question: Can an explicit generic spatial structure be analytically normalized so multiple deliberately different spatial hypotheses reproduce the P4AX 48-micrometre diffuse-rms amplitude, while remaining measurably spectrum-distinct and never relabeling a hypothesis as Kodak NPS?

compiler.aperture: normalized binary circular area kernel on the fixed physical grid

simulation.measurement_crop: exclude aperture radius plus spatial-kernel radius plus two samples on every edge

branch_rule.pass: Retain a generic aperture-normalization primitive and keep white/fine/coarse as explicit, non-selected spatial hypotheses. A separately evidenced source is still required to choose a spectrum before photographic or profile use.
branch_rule.fail: Close the compiler without changing kernels, field size, seeds, crop, error gates or spectrum probe.

forbidden: select a spatial hypothesis from this amplitude-only experiment
call any hypothesis Kodak grain, measured NPS, dye-cloud radius or scanner response
normalize each realized field from its observed output variance
fit kernels or amplitudes on photographs
render photographs or alter product defaults
claim_ceiling: Generic deterministic aperture-amplitude normalization and explicit demonstration that one diffuse-rms amplitude is compatible with multiple distinct spatial spectra; not measured Kodak NPS, causal grain structure, calibration or product evidence.
